subject: Tiered slab pricing exception + compact SOW amendment request
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@aurora-ai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tiered slab pricing exception & SOW adjustment

Hi Jordan / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo this week — feedback from our ML infra and product groups looks promising. We have a short procurement window to lock in pricing for Q3, and I'm reaching out with two asks that need to be reflected in an amendment rather than a fresh order form: 

1) Slab pricing exception: our usage forecast for the North America pilot is lumpy (50% of tokens concentrated in 3 burst windows). The standard tiered slab math overcharges us on the mid-tier. We'd like a temporary slab exception for the first 6 months that caps the effective per-token rate once cumulative usage exceeds 12M tokens per month.

2) SOW edit: we need a compact SOW appendix that clarifies integration windows and who owns the inference test events — Aurora will own the test harness, Redwood provides support and a single-engineer onboarding window (4 weeks).

I've attached our forecast and an annotated screenshot of the current order form. Can you confirm whether this is something Redwood can do via a short amendment/change-order? If so, please circulate a draft we can run through procurement.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Partnerships
Aurora AI

Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. We can definitely handle this as a limited-term amendment instead of redoing the entire order form. Next steps I propose: 

- I will attach a draft amendment (short form) that: 1) adds a 6-month slab exception clause with the cap you described, 2) appends the compact SOW appendix for onboarding responsibilities and timelines.
- Karthik, can you run the pricing calc and confirm the exact capped per-token number once Aurora confirms monthly baseline?
- Mina, our legal review will need the MSA/Order Form cross-references and the fallback language (what happens after 6 months). I've asked Jordan to loop you in — attaching a first-pass redline for clarity.

Sanjay, if this approach looks good to you I'll route the redline to Mina for legal markups; once we align, we'll push to DocuSign for signature. Expected internal turnaround: pricing calc same day, legal redline within 24–48 hours.

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tiered slab pricing exception & SOW adjustment

Jordan / Karthik / Sanjay — I reviewed the proposed short-form amendment (attached) and summarized required edits below. Quoted most relevant language and added inline notes to the attached PDF (legal-comments-aurora.pdf). High level: we can accept a 6-month slab exception, but we need explicit language for the following points before I can approve routing to DocuSign:

1) Post-term reversion: define the default billing behavior after month 6 (we suggest automatic transition to the standard tiered slab unless customer provides a 30-day notice to request extended exception).

2) Measurement window: clarify that monthly usage for slab triggers is calculated on a calendar-month basis and that Redwood's telemetry (token_count_v1) is the authoritative source; include a short dispute process (30 days to raise a usage dispute with evidence).

3) Audit & logs: because this exception impacts billing, Aurora must allow Redwood a one-time audit of aggregated usage logs for the exception period; scope limited to token counts and request timestamps.

4) SOW ownership & SLAs: the compact SOW needs a one-paragraph acceptance criteria for the onboarding test events (e.g., successful inference of canonical test suite within the onboarding window). If Aurora owns the harness, we need written confirmation in the SOW appendix that Redwood will not be responsible for client-side harness bugs.

5) Liability cap & indemnity: for a short-term commercial exception we can keep existing MSA caps but propose an explicit carve-out for misuse of burst pools (e.g., third-party traffic leeching) — brief language added in section 3 of the attached PDF.

If those items are acceptable, I'll prepare the final redline and send to Sanjay for internal review. Sanjay — to speed procurement, can you confirm: (a) Aurora's projected baseline monthly tokens for Q3 (we only need an approximate number for pricing calc), and (b) who on your side signs smaller amendments (title + email)? If the signer is procurement@aurora-ai.com we can route a condensed approval flow.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Inline attachments quoted: legal-comments-aurora.pdf (annotated redline), redline-amendment.docx (first-pass)

- Signatory: Aurora procurement (procurement@aurora-ai.com) signs amendments under $75k; for anything above that it goes to our Head of Finance (Lindsey Park). This one will likely be under the $75k threshold once Karthik confirms the capped per-token price.

We accept the post-term reversion and measurement window language in principle; one ask on the audit clause — Aurora requests that audits be limited to aggregated metrics and that Redwood coordinates a single 2-hour sync to review any flagged items instead of a full data pull. If you can add that constraint, we're comfortable proceeding to final redline and signature.

Please route the revised redline when ready and we'll aim to turn internally within 48 hours.
